Forecast Discussion

A strong fall cold front pushed through Friday evening, heralding the arrival of a much cooler air mass. Meanwhile, a strong upper level disturbance will pivot through this morning, keeping the winds gusty and maintaining a flow of Canadian air into the mountains.

Early drizzle or light rain will conclude, and skies will turn mostly sunny for the afternoon, as blustery northwest winds diminish somewhat. Across the highest elevations, some morning rime or flurries is not out of the question.

Under clear skies tonight, a more significant frost/freeze potential develops by daybreak as the winds subside. It’s that time of year.

Sunday skies are sunny with a continuation of cool temperatures. Under clear skies Sunday night, more valley frost is likely.

Next week, temperatures will moderate. While a slow-moving coastal cyclone batters sections of the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast Coast of the United States,  high pressure to west of this important feature will keep skies clear and temperatures just a tad above normal.
